hook.line: When Mariana writes up the assembly, "he said" tells readers nothing. Did he give in, hint, or dig in? Spanish has a verb for each, and picking it is how you show what you think of the quote.
hook.en: He admitted he had made a mistake.

examples.en: He admitted he had made a mistake.
He hinted that I had lied.
She maintained that she was innocent.

examples.es: El político aseguró que no sabía nada.
examples.en: The politician insisted he knew nothing.

examples.es: Mariana comentó que la votación fue injusta.
examples.en: Mariana remarked that the vote was unfair.

examples.es: El dueño declaró que no iba a vender.
examples.en: The owner declared that he wasn't going to sell.

rule:
*Dijo que* is neutral. A sharper verb tells us what the speaker was doing:

*Reconoció / admitió que*: gave in.
*Insinuó que*: hinted, never said it outright.
*Sostuvo / aseguró / afirmó que*: held firm.
*Comentó que*: remarked.
*Soltó que*: blurted it out.

Pick the verb as English picks "admitted" over "said". Then comes *que* and a normal statement, with no *de* before it: *sostuvo que*, never *sostuvo de que*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these verbs of saying with a stance: the verb itself carries your judgement of the quote.

options: He denied making a mistake.
He admitted he had made a mistake.
He boasted about a mistake.
He hinted that I had lied.
He swore that I had lied.
He asked whether I had lied.
She hoped she was innocent.
She admitted she wasn't innocent.
She maintained that she was innocent.

readAndPick.es: El político aseguró que no sabía nada.
options: The politician admitted he knew everything.
The politician insisted he knew nothing.
The politician asked what he should know.

readAndPick.es: Vale afirmó que la receta era suya.
options: Vale firmly stated the recipe was hers.
Vale doubted the recipe was hers.
Vale asked whether the recipe was hers.

readAndPick.es: Mariana comentó que la votación fue injusta.
options: Mariana shouted that the vote was unfair.
Mariana swore the vote was unfair.
Mariana remarked that the vote was unfair.

readAndPick.es: El funcionario admitió que el acta no estaba.
options: The official admitted the minutes weren't there.
The official insisted the minutes were there.
The official hinted the minutes weren't there.

readAndPick.es: Hernando mencionó que Altamira ya llamó.
options: Hernando denied that Altamira had called.
Hernando mentioned that Altamira had already called.
Hernando insisted that Altamira would call.

readAndPick.es: El dueño declaró que no iba a vender.
options: The owner hinted he might sell.
The owner admitted he was going to sell.
The owner declared he wasn't going to sell.

yourTurn.prompt: He admitted he had made a mistake. Choose *Reconoció* or *Insinuó*: ___ que se había equivocado.
yourTurn.why: *Reconoció* is giving in; *insinuó* is only hinting.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: He hinted that I had lied.
yourTurn.why: *Insinuó que* is the verb for saying something without quite saying it.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: She maintained that she was innocent.
yourTurn.why: *Sostuvo que* holds a position firmly, with no *de* before *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The politician insisted he knew nothing.
yourTurn.answer: El político aseguró que no sabía nada.
accept: El político aseguró que no sabía nada
El político afirmó que no sabía nada.
yourTurn.why: *Aseguró* and *afirmó* both mean he stood by the claim.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale firmly stated the recipe was hers.
yourTurn.answer: Vale afirmó que la receta era suya.
accept: Vale afirmó que la receta era suya
Vale aseguró que la receta era suya.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a remark instead of an insistence: Mariana aseguró que la votación fue injusta.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana comentó que la votación fue injusta.
accept: Mariana comentó que la votación fue injusta
yourTurn.why: *Comentó* is lighter than *aseguró*: she just remarked on it.

yourTurn.prompt: Change "said" to "admitted": El funcionario dijo que el acta no estaba.
yourTurn.answer: El funcionario admitió que el acta no estaba.
accept: El funcionario admitió que el acta no estaba
El funcionario reconoció que el acta no estaba.
yourTurn.why: Swap *dijo* for a verb of giving in and the rest stays the same.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Reporting verbs take *que* directly; there is no *de* before it.

pitfalls.wrong: Él dijo que reconoció que se había equivocado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Reconoció que* already means "he said, admitting", so you don't need *dijo que* as well.
Almost. If he never said it outright, *dijo* is too strong; *insinuó* says he only hinted.

personal: Think of someone who admitted something, or insisted on something, this week. Write it with a sharper verb than *dijo*: *Mi amigo reconoció que…*
